title: Dynamic onboarding credit curation and graduated upgrade paths
creator: Avery Chen
description: Hypothesis: A curated, usage-aware onboarding credit allocation with a graduated upgrade path (progressive unlocks and contextual upgrade prompts) will increase time-to-first-pay conversion and reduce early churn compared to a one-size-fits-all trial credit allocation. This ticket defines the experiment variants, measurement plan, and enterprise questionnaire impacts for negotiated contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment framework deployed for 3 variants with deterministic sample assignment
Instrumentation in place: cohort tagging, conversion funnel events, credit burn tracking, and first-bill revenue attribution
Dashboard showing daily cohort metrics and statistical significance estimates for primary metric
Product messaging copy and in-console upgrade prompt flows approved by design and legal
Enterprise contract/security questionnaire addendum drafted for negotiated trials that waive expiry or increase credit caps
experiment_plan: Population: new signups over 30-day window, excluding sandbox/test accounts and known SSO enterprise domains
A - Baseline: flat 1000 free credits, 30-day expiry, standard upgrade CTAs
B - Curated: onboarding survey collects intent tiers (prototype / evaluation / integration) and assigns credits 500/2000/10000 with 30-day expiry
C - Graduated unlocks: 500 initial credits + usage milestones that grant additional bundles (e.g., after 2 successful sessions grant +1000), contextual upgrade prompts tied to milestone completion
Sample size: target 25k new signups total (8.3k per arm) to detect 12% relative lift in conversion with 80% power
Duration: 30-day exposure + 60-day follow-up for revenue realization
Routing: deterministic by user_id hash stored in profile to ensure sticky assignment across devices
Failover: if kernel/usage infra incidents occur, pause enrollment and migrate recent signups to baseline
metrics: Primary: 60-day conversion to paid plan (first paid invoice issued)
Secondary: time-to-first-paid-invoice, average initial MRR, credit burn velocity, 30/60-day churn of converted users
Safety guardrails: percentage hitting credit cap within 7 days, number of support tickets related to credits, fraud/abuse signals
rollout_schedule: Week 0: finalize variant copy, design, legal checklist, and instrumentation plan
Week 1: implement assignment logic and backend credit API changes (ENG feature flag gated)
Week 2: QA + internal dogfood, design review of in-console prompts, privacy/legal signoff
Week 3: ramp to 100% of new signups, monitor live metrics daily
Week 7: interim analysis, decide whether to extend or iterate; full analysis after follow-up period
risks: Enterprise sales friction if public trial sizes undercut negotiated commitments; must add clear addendum for contract trials
Higher credit caps may increase short-term cost if caching/batching not correctly applied; coordinate with Optimize team
Complexity in milestone-based unlocks could confuse users without clear UI affordances
Potential for gaming/fraud (multiple accounts); need rate limits and detection rules from infra/security
decisions: Use deterministic hashing for variant assignment to maintain user continuity
Milestone unlocks will be implemented as server-side credit grants with event audit logs
Enterprise deals will include a standardized trial addendum template (legal to produce) to opt out of public expiry rules
A/B analysis will use both frequentist and Bayesian estimates; conversion primary test will require pre-registered analysis plan
